dryRun.sidebar: Dry run: nothing will be moved

smart.subtitle: Scan everything that can be cleaned in one go
smart.heroTitle: Give your Mac a full check-up
smart.heroHint: Scans system junk, developer junk, leftovers, downloads, large files and the Trash (the Trash needs Full Disk Access). Scanning only reads; nothing is changed.

space.subtitle: See where your disk space went
space.heroHint: Measures the space each folder actually uses on the internal data volume, counting hard links once. Usually takes under a minute; a few minutes on Macs with very many files.

system.subtitle: App caches, logs, crash reports and temporary files
system.heroHint: Caches are rebuilt automatically when needed. Caches of running apps and files in use are not selected, and are skipped again when cleaning.

dev.subtitle: npm, pip, Homebrew and Docker caches, idle node_modules
dev.heroHint: Package caches can be downloaded again at any time. Only node_modules of projects untouched for a while are listed.

large.subtitle: Find big files and files you haven't used in a long time
large.heroHint: Scans your whole home folder, including hidden folders and ~/Library. Protected locations, Git repository internals, build output, virtual environments and app bundle contents are skipped. Nothing is selected by default; you decide.

apps.subtitle: Remove apps completely, including their related files

leftovers.subtitle: Settings, caches and data left behind by removed apps
leftovers.heroHint: Compares bundle IDs with installed apps to find files that no longer have an owner.

trash.subtitle: Empty the Trash and tidy up Downloads
trash.heroHint: Installers that have been in Downloads for over a month are suggested for cleaning.

history.subtitle: A record of every clean-up, stored only on this Mac

settings.subtitle: Language, appearance, safety and cleaning rules

errors.outsideAllowed: Outside the areas that may be cleaned
errors.tooShallow: This is a top-level folder; only its contents can be cleaned
errors.changed: The file changed since the scan, please rescan
errors.finderFailed: Finder couldn't move this item (the password prompt may have been cancelled)
errors.brewFailed: brew uninstall failed; moved to the Trash instead
errors.appRefusedQuit: The app didn't quit (it may have unsaved documents); uninstall stopped
errors.insidePackage: This is inside an app, library or document package, or a Git repository's .git folder; it can only be removed as a whole
errors.inUse: The file is in use, skipped
errors.oldRunning: The installed version didn't quit; quit it and try again
errors.oldNotMoved: Couldn't move the installed version to the Trash
errors.copyFailed: Copying to Applications failed. If the old version was moved to the Trash, you can put it back
errors.locked: The file is locked (Locked is checked in Finder's Get Info), skipped
errors.restoreExists: Something with the same name is already at the original location, skipped
errors.restoreNotInTrash: This item is no longer in the Trash
errors.restoreManual: No Trash location was recorded; put it back in Finder

confirm.title: Confirm clean-up
confirm.desc_one: {{count}} item, {{size}}. Uncheck anything you want to keep.
confirm.desc_other: {{count}} items, {{size}} in total. Uncheck anything you want to keep.
confirm.emptyDesc: {{size}} in this Mac's Trash will be deleted permanently.
confirm.dryRunNote: Dry run is on: items are only listed, nothing is moved or deleted. You can turn it off in Settings.
confirm.trashNote: Files and folders go to the Trash and can be put back until you empty it.
confirm.emptyWarning: This can't be undone. The files can't be recovered. Trash on external drives is emptied too.
confirm.permanentNote: Includes command items (brew cleanup / docker prune). They delete permanently, without the Trash.
confirm.adminNote: Some items belong to the administrator; Finder will ask for your password.

result.dryTitle: Dry run finished, nothing was moved
result.dryDesc_one: With dry run off, this item would be moved to the Trash.
result.dryDesc_other: With dry run off, these {{count}} items would be moved to the Trash.
result.trashHint_one: {{count}} item moved to the Trash. Space is freed once you empty the Trash.
result.trashHint_other: {{count}} items moved to the Trash. Space is freed once you empty the Trash.
result.dryEmptyDesc: With dry run off, the Trash would be emptied permanently.
result.dryCmdDesc_one: {{count}} command item would run and delete directly.
result.dryCmdDesc_other: {{count}} command items would run and delete directly.

perm.missing: Not granted: the Trash, some leftovers and system folders can't be read

leftovers.fdaHint: With Full Disk Access, other apps' sandbox containers can be checked to find more leftovers.
leftovers.empty: No leftovers from removed apps were found.

trash.hint: Files in the Trash still use disk space until it is emptied.
trash.locked: Full Disk Access is needed to look inside the Trash
trash.downloadsHint: Installers older than a month are selected by default.

apps.search: Search by name or bundle ID

blockedHint.systemExtension: This app installs a system extension (usually security or network software). Use its own uninstaller.
blockedHint.protected: This app is in a protected location or your whitelist.

apps.pickHint: See its related files and remove it completely.
apps.willQuit: {{name}} is running. It will be asked to quit before uninstalling.
apps.brewUninstall: After the app is moved to the Trash, brew uninstall --cask {{token}} runs to update Homebrew's records. If the cask has uninstall steps, Homebrew runs them too.

space.fdaHint: With Full Disk Access the numbers will be more complete.
space.stale: The chart is from the last scan. Rescan to refresh it.
space.basketHint: Check removable items to move them to the Trash

smart.foundHint: Only the safe items selected by default. Review large files and the Trash separately.

settings.dryRunHint: When on, clean-ups only list what would be removed. Nothing is moved.
settings.whitelistHint: These paths and everything below them are never cleaned and are skipped by the cleaning modules. Space Lens still counts their size but can't delete them. Entries marked “Default” are built-in personal-data locations; you can remove them. You can also right-click items in the cleaning lists.
settings.appUnusedHint: Apps not opened for this long are flagged (never selected automatically).
settings.nodeModulesHint: Listed only when nothing at the top of the project (or of its Git repository) has changed for this long.
settings.nodeModulesRootsHint: Searched below these folders. ~/Library, ~/Applications, the Trash and hidden folders are always excluded; only node_modules next to a package.json count.
settings.aboutText: Runs locally. No network access, no data collection.
settings.dryRunOffDesc: Confirmed items will then really be moved to the Trash; command items (brew cleanup, docker prune) delete directly. Review a few dry runs before turning it off.
settings.removeDefaultDesc: {{path}} is a built-in personal-data location. Once removed, its files appear in Large Files and Space Lens and can be moved to the Trash.

history.emptyHint: Every clean-up and dry run is recorded here.
history.clearDesc: Only the records are removed. No files are affected.
history.restoreDesc_one: Move the {{count}} item this clean-up moved to the Trash back to where it was. Nothing at the original location is overwritten.
history.restoreDesc_other: Move the {{count}} items this clean-up moved to the Trash back to where they were. Anything already at the original location is skipped, never overwritten.
history.skippedTitle_one: {{count}} item skipped: a newer copy is already at the original location
history.skippedTitle_other: {{count}} items skipped: a newer copy is already at the original location
history.supersededHint: These were recreated by their apps after the clean-up. The new copy stays in place; the old copy stays in the Trash and is safe to empty.

onboarding.title: Welcome to MacCleaner
onboarding.subtitle: Before you start, here is how it keeps your files safe
onboarding.trashText: Cleaned files go to the Trash, so mistakes can be put back. A few command items (brew, Docker) delete directly; you are warned before confirming.
onboarding.dryText: See what would be cleaned first. Turn it off in Settings when you're happy.
onboarding.safeText: System files and Keychains are never cleaned. Documents, Mail, iCloud and other personal data are protected by default; adjust in Settings.
onboarding.fda1: Click “Open System Settings” and go to Privacy & Security → Full Disk Access
onboarding.fda2: Turn on the switch next to MacCleaner (click “+” to add it if missing)
onboarding.fda3: Come back and click “Check again”; restart MacCleaner if needed

desc.fresh: MacCleaner is running from outside the Applications folder. After installing it reopens from Applications.
desc.upgrade: The installed version is moved to the Trash (you can put it back), then this version is installed and reopened. Settings, whitelist and history are kept.
desc.reinstall: The same version is already installed. Continuing moves it to the Trash, installs this copy and reopens. Settings, whitelist and history are kept.
desc.downgrade: The installed version is newer than this copy. Continuing moves it to the Trash and installs this older version. Settings, whitelist and history are kept.
desc.conflict: Applications already contains a MacCleaner.app that isn't MacCleaner. Deal with it first, then open this copy again.

install.downgradeWarning: An older version may lack fixes from the newer one.
